t: Of the funds appropriated under this head in the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1980 (Public Law 96–126) and previous Interior Department Appropriations Acts $165,000,000 shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980, of which $75,000,000 is available for payments to the States; $18,200,000 is available to the Forest Service; $13,775,000 is available to the United States Fish and Wildlife Service; $52,025,000 is available to the National Park Service; and $6,000,000 is available for land acquisition at Pinelands National Reserve: Provided, That $2,250,000 of the amount set aside for contingencies shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980.

fable.w: This provision only defers and allocates previously appropriated funds among the States and federal agencies (Forest Service, Fish and Wildlife Service, National Park Service). The tempting reading is that "payments to the States" brings an outside party in, but that is a funding allocation, not consultation, a hearing, a comment process, or a right to sue over a federal decision. No outside party takes part in any federal decision here.
fable.s: $75,000,000 is available for payments to the States

qwen_block.w: This section is a standard appropriations provision that dictates when specific funds become available for obligation and how they are allocated among federal agencies and for payments to states. It does not require any consultation, coordination, or participation by outside parties in the decision-making process regarding these funds. The mention of 'payments to the States' refers to the disbursement of funds, not a participatory process in a federal decision.
qwen_block.s: Of the funds appropriated under this head in the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1980 (Public Law 96–126) and previous Interior Department Appropriations Acts $165,000,000 shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980, of which $75,000,000 is available for payments to the States; $18,200,000 is available to the Forest Service; $13,775,000 is available to the United States Fish and Wildlife Service; $52,025,000 is available to the National Park Service; and $6,000,000 is available for land acquisition at Pinelands National Reserve: Provided, That $2,250,000 of the amount set aside for contingencies shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980.

opus.w: This section only says when appropriated funds become available and how they are split among recipients. "Payments to the States" might look like it involves outside parties. But receiving funds is like getting a grant or benefit, and states are not consulted on any federal decision. Nothing in the section creates a hearing, comment period, advisory body, consultation requirement, or right to sue.
opus.s: $165,000,000 shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980, of which $75,000,000 is available for payments to the States

qwen_chat.w: This section details the allocation and availability of appropriated funds to various federal agencies and states. It does not require consultation, coordination, or input from any outside party (such as the general public, non-federal experts, or local governments) before a federal decision is made. The mention of payments to states is a financial transfer, not a participatory process in decision-making.
qwen_chat.s: Of the funds appropriated under this head in the Interior and Related Agencies Appropriation Act, 1980 (Public Law 96–126) and previous Interior Department Appropriations Acts $165,000,000 shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980, of which $75,000,000 is available for payments to the States; $18,200,000 is available to the Forest Service; $13,775,000 is available to the United States Fish and Wildlife Service; $52,025,000 is available to the National Park Service; and $6,000,000 is available for land acquisition at Pinelands National Reserve: Provided, That $2,250,000 of the amount set aside for contingencies shall not become available for obligation until October 1, 1980.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that allocating funds to States implies some form of coordination or participation. However, the text merely specifies the availability and allocation of appropriated funds. It does not require the federal government to consult with states, the public, or any outside entity before making a decision. The allocation is a unilateral executive/appropriative action.
